label: <DEL> step of long sequences starting with 2 (or l)
explanation: Fires almost only at the delimiter step (95% of mass; never in the copy phase; a weak trickle on the last 1-3 original tokens of the same sequences). It needs long sequences (L >= 6, rate rising with L) and depends strongly on the first original token, which is the token about to be output: first token 2 holds 76% of mass (20x lift) and l holds 13%. Activations are larger when n or w appear early (orig(1)/orig(2), e.g. 2 n ..., 2 w ..., l n n w ...), and when the token just before <DEL> is e/b/j. The predicate covers 84% of mass on dev but has low precision (about 6%): most delimiter steps of long 2-initial sequences stay silent. Adding an n/w-early condition raises precision to about 28% but lowers mass recall to 0.57. Does not fire on short sequences (L <= 4), on copy-phase steps, or on sequences starting with other tokens beyond a small tail (o, 1, k).
